item.title: The Punishment for Peacekeepers Raping Haitian Children Was Dismissal
item.description: Decades after soldiers in Sri Lanka’s military were accused of sexually abusing minors while some of the troops were serving as United Nations peacekeepers in Haiti, the Sri Lankan government recently acknowledged that they were tried internally by a Sri Lankan military court, convicted and punished by dismissal. item.title: Gaza: At least 20 killed in deadly building collapse, search for survivors continues
item.description: Search and rescue operations continued in Gaza City on Wednesday following the collapse of a bombed-out building that killed at least 20 people, according to reports.

item.title: The world comes to New York: What’s at stake at UN General Assembly high-level week
item.description: Each September, New York becomes the centre of global diplomacy as presidents, prime ministers, ministers and diplomats from around the world gather at United Nations Headquarters.

item.title: AI, climate and conflicts top Guterres’s agenda ahead of General Assembly
item.description: Ahead of the UN General Assembly’s high-level week, Secretary-General António Guterres said the world had entered “an era of deep uncertainty” and urged governments to embrace international cooperation to address global threats.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: ‘Being a woman is a crime in Afghanistan,’ civil society briefer declares
item.description: Since the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021, the continuing presence of terrorist groups as well as rights violations against women and girls are a growing concern as the Security Council meets Wednesday to hear the latest updates, including from a civil society representative who said being born as a woman in the country “is a crime”.

item.title: UN report warns of reprisals against those who collaborate in defence of human rights
item.description: Activists, lawyers and others who cooperate with the United Nations on human rights continue to face intimidation and reprisals, according to a new report issued on Wednesday by the Secretary-General that calls for greater protection and accountability.

item.title: World News in Brief: Shipping alert from IMO, democracy vanishing in Nicaragua, alert over political ‘denialism’
item.description: Amid a rising number of attacks on shipping in key waterways in the Middle East linked to the US-Iran war, the head of UN maritime agency, Mr. Arsenio Dominguez, has insisted that the conflict is not a “pretext” to target “innocent seafarers”.

item.title: Repression continues in Venezuela in the face of ‘appalling’ human rights violations
item.description: In Venezuela’s El Rodeo maximum security prison, some of those detained for political reasons are subject to forced intubation – and prolonged confinement in a sealed underground cistern.

item.title: Who should set the rules for AI? The UN is pushing for a safer digital future
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing rapidly, raising questions about how societies and governments can capture its benefits while managing risks that often extend beyond national borders.

item.title: African Farmers Demand Affordable Finance as Governments Fall Short on Funding
item.description: Agriculture remains underfunded in Africa as governments struggle to deliver on decades-old promises to dedicate 10% of national income to agriculture. But for many farmers, mobilising finance is only half the battle. Reaching smallholder farmers in the last mile with the little available finance remains a challenge. item.title: Killing of Environmental Defenders Reflects Power Struggle Over World’s Resources
item.description: At least 124 land and environmental defenders were killed around the world in 2025 while protecting forests, rivers, farmland and Indigenous territories, according to a new report by Global Witness that warns violence against activists remains widespread even as recorded killings have declined from previous years. item.title: One Man’s Quest to End Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) in Mali
item.description: After years of defending FGM as a cultural practice, Sidi Haidara came to a realization: No tradition should come at the expense of a girl’s health, rights, or future.

item.title: Renewed Hostilities In Yemen Inflame Displacement and Regional Risks
item.description: In recent days, the humanitarian situation in Yemen has deteriorated sharply following a new escalation of hostilities between the Iran-backed Houthi rebels and the Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council (PLC). This follows four years of relative stability, marking the most severe resurgence of violence since the collapse of the United Nations (UN)-mediated ceasefire in October 2022. […]
